# Part 1: R

## 1. Reaction times

```{r}
rt <- c(523, 487, 601, 455, 2310, 512, 498, 577, 466, 540)
condition <- c("easy", "hard", "hard", "easy", "hard",
               "easy", "hard", "hard", "easy", "easy")

length(rt)
mean(rt); median(rt); min(rt); max(rt)
which.max(rt)   # trial 5: far slower than the rest. The median is robust to it, the mean is not.
```

```{r}
keep <- rt < 2000            # one logical vector subsets both, so they stay aligned
rt_clean <- rt[keep]
cond_clean <- condition[keep]
mean(rt_clean)

mean(rt_clean[cond_clean == "easy"])
mean(rt_clean[cond_clean == "hard"])

rt_s <- rt / 1000
```

## 2. Missing trials

```{r}
rt2 <- c(523, NA, 487, 150, 601, 455, 2310, NA, 512, 498)

sum(is.na(rt2)); which(is.na(rt2))
mean(rt2, na.rm = TRUE)

implausible <- rt2 < 200 | rt2 > 1500    # NA where rt2 is NA
sum(implausible, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(implausible, na.rm = TRUE)          # proportion of the non-missing trials
```

```{r}
rt2[rt2 > 200]     # NA > 200 is NA, so each NA trial returns an NA
rt2_ok <- rt2[!is.na(rt2) & rt2 >= 200 & rt2 <= 1500]
rt2_ok
```

## 3. Spot the bugs

```{r}
scores <- c(12, 15, 9, 20, 17)
group <- c("a", "b", "a", "b", "a")
mean(scores[group == "a"])   # = instead of ==, and a missing )
mean(scores[group == "b"])   # maen
mean(scores)                 # Mean: R is case-sensitive
summary(scores)              # Scores
```

The silent one is `=` instead of `==`. Inside `[ ]`, `group = "a"` does not compare anything: R reads it as `scores["a"]`, the element named `"a"`. There is none, so you get `NA` and no error.

## 4. A Likert item

```{r}
answers <- c("often", "never", "sometimes", "always", "often", "rarely",
             "sometimes", "often", "never", "always", "sometimes", "often")
table(answers)     # alphabetical: "always" comes first

lev <- c("never", "rarely", "sometimes", "often", "always")
answers_f <- factor(answers, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
table(answers_f)

score <- as.numeric(answers_f)
mean(score)
```

```{r}
factor(c(answers, "Often"), levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
```

`"Often"` is not one of the levels (case-sensitive), so it becomes `NA`, silently. Check with `sum(is.na(...))` after building a factor.

## 5. A data frame by hand

```{r}
participants <- data.frame(
  id    = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06"),
  group = factor(c("patient", "control", "patient", "control", "patient", "control")),
  age   = c(72, 65, 68, 70, 61, 74),
  score = c(21, 29, 23, 28, 25, 27)
)
str(participants)

participants$low_score <- participants$score < 24
participants[participants$group == "patient" & participants$age > 65, ]
mean(participants$score[participants$group == "patient"])
mean(participants$score[participants$group == "control"])
participants[order(participants$age), ]
```

## 6. Your first functions

```{r}
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))   # length() would count the NA
}
se(rt_clean)
se(rt2)

n_outliers <- function(x, low = 200, high = 1500) {
  sum(x < low | x > high, na.rm = TRUE)
}
n_outliers(rt2)
n_outliers(rt2, high = 600)   # 601 now counts too
```

## 7. A drug trial: `sleep`

```{r}
str(sleep)        # 20 rows, 3 columns: each patient appears twice
head(sleep)
summary(sleep)
mean(sleep$extra[sleep$group == "1"])
mean(sleep$extra[sleep$group == "2"])

# both groups list the patients in the same ID order (check sleep$ID), so we can subtract
d21 <- sleep$extra[sleep$group == "2"] - sleep$extra[sleep$group == "1"]
sum(d21 > 0)
```

## 8. Sleep deprivation: `sleepstudy`

```{r}
sleepstudy <- read.csv(here::here("data", "sleepstudy.csv"))
length(unique(sleepstudy$Subject))
rt_base <- mean(sleepstudy$Reaction[sleepstudy$Days == 2])
rt9 <- mean(sleepstudy$Reaction[sleepstudy$Days == 9])
c(rt_base, rt9)
```

```{r}
base <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 2, ]
day9 <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 9, ]
all(base$Subject == day9$Subject)    # same order: safe to subtract

change <- day9$Reaction - base$Reaction
sum(change > 0)
base$Subject[which.max(change)]
hist(change)
```

# Part 2: Quarto

## 9. Your first report

A table of contents appears in a left sidebar. All HTML options: <https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html>.

```markdown
### My project

I study **sleep** in *university students* using:

- questionnaires
- a sleep diary
- reaction times

More on the [Quarto website](https://quarto.org).
```

## 10. Bring in your analysis

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| echo: false
sleepstudy <- read.csv(here::here("data", "sleepstudy.csv"))
```

```{{r}}
base <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 2, ]
day9 <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 9, ]
change <- day9$Reaction - base$Reaction
```

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-change
#| fig-cap: "Change in reaction time from baseline (day 2) to day 9, one value per subject."
hist(change, xlab = "Change in reaction time (ms)", main = NULL)
```
````

```{r}
#| label: fig-change
#| fig-cap: "Change in reaction time from baseline (day 2) to day 9, one value per subject."
#| echo: false
hist(change, xlab = "Change in reaction time (ms)", main = NULL)
```

`@fig-change` becomes a numbered, clickable "Figure 1". With `echo: false` the chunk still runs, but its code is hidden. This chunk prints nothing, so it disappears from the report.

## 11. Numbers in the text

```markdown
After 7 nights with 3 hours in bed, reaction time increased by `{{r}} round(mean(change))` ms
on average; `{{r}} sum(change > 0)` of `{{r}} length(change)` subjects slowed down (@fig-change).
```

> After 7 nights with 3 hours in bed, reaction time increased by `{r} round(mean(change))` ms on average; `{r} sum(change > 0)` of `{r} length(change)` subjects slowed down (@fig-change).

```markdown
On average, patients slept `{{r}} round(mean(d21), 2)` hours more with drug 2 than with drug 1,
and `{{r}} sum(d21 > 0)` out of 10 slept more with drug 2.
```

> On average, patients slept `{r} round(mean(d21), 2)` hours more with drug 2 than with drug 1, and `{r} sum(d21 > 0)` out of 10 slept more with drug 2.

## 12. Does it render from scratch?

Render fails: `object 'x' not found`. Rendering starts a fresh R session that never saw the console. Everything the document needs must be created **inside** it. After *Restart R* the document still renders: it is self-contained.

```{r}
sessionInfo()
```

## Bonus

Same text, figure and numbers in all three: one source, three outputs. The PDF and the Word file have no table of contents, because `toc` sits under `html:` only. The Word file can be edited, e.g. by a co-author, but edits there are lost at the next render: change the `.qmd` instead.
